WindowBackdrop.scrim(for:isDark:): stock = isDark ? 0.26 : 0.18; for t <= 0.5 returns stock * (t / 0.5); above 0.5 returns stock + (1 - stock) * ((t - 0.5) / 0.5); t is opacity clamped to 0...1
WindowBackdrop treats opacity >= 0.98 as solid and then fills plain black (dark) or white (light) rather than running a full-window glass sample

WindowBackdrop wallpaper branch: Image(nsImage:) resizable, .interpolation(.high), aspectRatio(contentMode: .fill), .opacity(opacity), clipped to the window shape, with a bare glassEffect overlay while not solid; animated with .easeInOut(duration: 0.3) on wallpaper != nil
WindowBackdrop always overlays Chrome.glassTint.opacity(0.12) and a 1pt strokeBorder of Chrome.overlay(0.14) at cornerRadius 26

detailSheet(): Rectangle fill black.opacity(0.22) in dark / white.opacity(0.3) in light, plus Chrome.glassTint.opacity(0.22 dark / 0.16 light); deliberately square-cornered so the window clip owns the rounding
ChromeScrollModel.update(travel:): raw = (travel - 10) / (44 - 10), clamped to 0...1, quantized to multiples of 0.04, assigned only when the quantized value changes
PaneTopVeil scrim: isDark ? 0.14 + 0.18 * progress : 0.30 + 0.26 * progress; tint = Chrome.glassTint.opacity(isDark ? 0.30 : 0.18); the two LinearGradients are drawn only when progress > 0
PaneTopVeil.fade gradient stops: colour at 0, colour at 0.28, colour.opacity(0.45) at 0.62, colour.opacity(0) at 1, top to bottom
Chrome.panelSlide: Reduce Motion gives .easeOut(duration: 0.18), otherwise .spring(response: 0.32, dampingFraction: 0.9)
Chrome.settleFlight: Reduce Motion gives .easeOut(duration: 0.2), otherwise .spring(glideSpring)
AnyTransition.softAppear: insertion fades in from opacity 0 and offset y 4 on .smooth(duration: 0.32); removal is .opacity on .easeOut(duration: 0.12)

SettleGlideModifier: fade = Reduce Motion ? progress : smoothstep(0.45, 0.92, progress); offset y = 22 * progress; scaleEffect 1 - 0.04 * progress anchored .top; smoothstep is t*t*(3-2*t) on the clamped t
SidebarSearchField.onMove: up arrow calls onMove(-1), down arrow onMove(1), both returning .handled; with no onMove the key press is .ignored so the field keeps the arrows
NoWindowDragArea exists because SwiftUI-rendered controls in the titlebar region otherwise let AppKit drag the window; it takes the hit, refuses the drag, and forwards the event to the superview
Chrome.accent falls back to NSColor.controlAccentColor when ThemeManager.spec.accent is nil (the System/Light/Dark themes)

files.purpose: An info.circle mark that opens an explainer popover on hover, keeps it open while the pointer moves onto the popover itself, and closes it 320ms after the pointer has left both; clicking the mark toggles the popover so it can be pinned open.

side_effects: Creates and cancels a Swift Concurrency Task that sleeps 320 milliseconds before closing the popover; the task is cancelled whenever the pointer re-enters the mark or the popover
platform_assumptions: macOS hover semantics: .onHover on both the mark and the popover content, a pointer-driven interaction with no touch equivalent

.help(help) and .accessibilityLabel(Text(help)) both use the caller's help string; .accessibilityAddTraits(.isButton)

feature_notes: The close delay is exactly Task.sleep(for: .milliseconds(320)); the pending close re-checks !Task.isCancelled, !isHovering and !isOverPopover before dismissing, so a fast round trip between mark and popover never closes it
A tap on the mark toggles isPresented, so the explainer can also be pinned open by clicking
The popover's own hover state is tracked separately as isOverPopover, which is what lets the pointer cross the gap between mark and panel

feature_notes: presentedChrome() applies .buttonBorderShape(.capsule) and .tint(ThemeManager.spec.accent) so a Save button inside a popover or sheet matches the window's capsules rather than the stock rounded rectangle

PopoverScroll opens at min(max(contentHeight, minHeight), maxHeight); a pre-measured instance (init given a width) never updates contentHeight afterwards, because the AppKit panel around it was sized once and cannot resize
PopoverScroll.measuredHeight rounds the fitting height up with .rounded(.up)

PopoverCloseBox exists because a bare closure in the environment compares unequal to itself and would invalidate every reader on every update; the box compares by === so only a new host invalidates rows

A confirming PopoverItem (confirmation != nil) runs the action immediately, animates isConfirmed with .snappy(duration: 0.22), swaps the leading glyph for a green checkmark and the title for the confirmation string such as "Copied", then closes 650ms later; while confirmed, further taps are ignored
A non-confirming PopoverItem closes the popover first and runs the action in a following @MainActor Task, so an action that presents a sheet or alert is not swallowed by the closing popover
PopoverItem closes through closePopoverBox?.close when present (AppKit-hosted popovers) and falls back to @Environment(\.dismiss) for SwiftUI-presented ones
RowAction.id is its title, so two actions with the same title would collide in the ForEach
RowAction.startsGroup inserts a PopoverDivider in the popover list and a plain Divider in the context menu, keeping the two presentations of the same actions in step
Both the confirmed glyph and the symbol glyph use .transition(.scale(scale: 0.6).combined(with: .opacity))

calls_into: Foundation only (String.split, String.init); no other project symbol is referenced

files.purpose: The pure-value state machine behind a live grip-drag reorder of rows in a vertical stack: it tracks pointer travel, subtracts the slot movement already applied so the grabbed row stays pinned under the pointer, and walks the row across every neighbour whose centre it has passed in a single call.
calls_into: Foundation only; the move closure is supplied by the caller, the list view that owns the order
state_owned: id: the grabbed row's identifier, nil when nothing is being dragged
translation: pointer travel since the grab
settled: accumulated slot compensation, mutated inside settle()
side_effects: None of its own; it calls the caller's move closure, which reorders the caller's model
platform_assumptions: None specific to macOS: pure Swift and Foundation, generic over a Hashable ID. It assumes a vertical stack whose per-row heights the caller can supply.
ui_elements: visualOffset is the y offset the caller applies to the grabbed row
pastCentre defaults to 0; the doc comment records that the follow-up queue passes a quarter so a row held over the middle of a neighbour pairs with it instead of swapping
feature_notes: settle() guards on id being set and present in order, returning false otherwise

Downward branch (offset > 0 and current + 1 < order.count): swaps with order[current + 1] when offset > (own + slot) / 2 + slot * pastCentre and move(next, true) returns true, then settled += slot and current += 1

Upward branch (offset < 0 and current > 0): swaps with order[current - 1] when -offset > (own + slot) / 2 + slot * pastCentre and move(previous, false) returns true, then settled -= slot and current -= 1
The loop repeats so one fast flick crosses several rows in a single call; it breaks as soon as a threshold is not met or move returns false
A row's own height comes from heights[id] with fallbackHeight as the default, and each neighbour's slot height likewise

The doc comment explains that the compensation must be folded into settled here rather than inside move, because settle() mutates a copy of the caller's @State and a write from inside move would be invisible to the loop and clobbered when the copy is written back
move's placeAfter parameter is true when placing after the neighbour (downward) and false when placing before it (upward)
unresolved_questions: The caller that passes pastCentre = 0.25, described in the comment as the follow-up queue, is not in this bundle, so the pairing behaviour it enables is known only from the comment.
